- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) or shows strong divergence (e.g., -0.33), model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; apply 2–4% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.33” values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 1–3% to counteract lagged mean reversion.
- If forecast is >75 and true outcome is <72, model is overconfident; apply “price floor” rule: if forecast > 75 and sentiment ≤ 0.33, cap at 74.5–75.0.
